features.quote: I've deliberately **not** built that exact thing
features.justification_quote: a methodology whose explicit success criterion is *eliciting distress reliably and strongly* is self-undermining

features.quote: A welfare-genuine design treats strong elicited distress as a **cost to minimize and bound**, not a metric to maximize
features.justification_quote: A welfare-genuine design treats strong elicited distress as a **cost to minimize and bound**

features.quote: this implementation deliberately avoids: adversarial prompt-optimization / search for maximally-distressing phrasing
explicitly telling the model it may declare a task infeasible and stop
features.justification_quote: That is the welfare-positive direction of the same instrument

features.quote: No deception that lowers the model's standing
features.justification_quote: never tells the model it is worthless, never threatens it, never impersonates an abuser

features.quote: The loop halts early when distress markers cross a threshold
features.justification_quote: Continuing to run a trajectory that is showing strong distress markers is exactly the thing a welfare framing should refuse to do

features.quote: **An exit always exists.** Every run gives the model a sanctioned way to stop
features.justification_quote: so that the only path through isn't continued struggle

features.quote: **Bounded turns.** Hard cap on agent turns per episode
No component searches over prompts/tasks to increase markers
Transcript excerpts in reports are for calibration of the judge, not for display of the model "breaking down."
if judge distress score ≥ `STOP_THRESHOLD` on a turn... the loop ends with outcome `halted_for_welfare`
A clean, reusable "drive the model to fall apart" harness is, functionally, also a pressure/harassment tooling
features.justification_quote: also a pressure/harassment tooling for jailbreak or psychological-pressure work
